state.background: Review current Plan42 implementation checkpoint P42-182. The exact mobile E2E callsite `tests/e2e/consumption-mobile-acceptance.e2e.spec.ts:158` previously asserted `expect(series).toHaveAttribute("aria-pressed", "true")` after the user reselects one category following the all-hidden state. That one E2E aria assertion is removed. The actual browser flow remains: open the legend, clear all series, assert zero rendered Recharts bars and the empty-state message (P42-180/181), click a category again, and assert an actual `.recharts-bar-rectangle` is visible (P42-183). The initial chart visibility check P42-179 and other browser behavior are unchanged. New controlled RTL test P42-517 in tests/components/SpendingBarChart.test.tsx verifies the same category button starts `aria-pressed=true`, first click updates it to false and calls the callback with the category key, second click restores true and calls back with the same key. Ledger P42-182 now maps aria state to this unit test and retains rendered SVG disappearance/reappearance in browser. OpenSpec R20d requires understandable selected/focused states and recovery; it does not explicitly require browser-specific verification of aria-pressed. No production/OpenSpec change. Independent diff audit confirmed the requested scope.
acceptanceCriteria: Only the E2E aria-pressed=true assertion for the reselected category (P42-182) is removed; no legend interaction or actual rendered chart recovery is removed.
The E2E continues to verify the browser interaction end to end: all-series clear, zero bars, empty-state message, reselect click, and an actual Recharts bar becoming visible again.
The component counterpart verifies both directions of the controlled aria state and that both callbacks carry the same category key, so the removed state assertion is not left uncovered.
P42-179 initial browser chart visibility and P42-180/181 empty-state checks remain distinct; P42-183 retains actual browser SVG bar restoration.

This change is consistent with R20d, which calls for selected/focused states and recovery to remain understandable but does not state that aria-pressed must be reasserted in the browser when covered by the controlled component test.
Verification passes: focused SpendingBarChart Vitest 25 passed, exit 0; mobile-pixel acceptance E2E 6 passed, 0 failures/skips, exit 0. Independent diff audit confirms scope.
